memory_update.text: LW is the primary US-listed direct frozen potato / French fry processor to track for the node; verify whether customer concentration, volume recovery, and plant utilization support or refute the operational-leverage thesis.
JBTM is a second-order underfollowed equipment candidate for potato-processing, frying, freezing, filtration, automation, and aftermarket exposure; potato-specific backlog evidence is required.
PFGC and USFD are distributor mappings, not processor chokepoints; they may reveal frozen-food throughput, fill-rate, and private-brand signals but require SKU-level evidence before upgrading.

Major direct fry processors McCain, Simplot, and Cavendish are not straightforward US-listed common-equity candidates, so the public-market expansion should search harder for adjacent equipment, cold-chain, packaging, potato-input, and private-label distribution proxies.

node: Frozen potato products and French fry supply
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around frozen potato and French fry supply with a two-lane funnel. Lamb Weston is the clearest direct public reference asset and is also within the preferred mid-cap hunting range at current market cap. The underfollowed lane is thin because several major fry processors are private, notably McCain and Simplot; therefore second-order public mappings matter: JBT Marel as processing/freezing/frying equipment, and Performance Food Group / US Foods as foodservice distribution channels where frozen foods and chain-restaurant fulfillment can transmit demand, logistics, and menu-consistency constraints. No buy/sell recommendation is implied.
